evidence: WHAT HOLDS (core of row 34). The product is interactive and time-varying (live board and conversation updates within 15 s, scroll-preserving earlier-message loading, drafts, optimistic move with put-back, session expiry) but explicitly not responsive or themed: instruction.md:11 'A clear desktop workspace is what matters. We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' and scored/visual/prompt.md:14 'Assess desktop craft at a conventional desktop viewport. No phone layout or theme switching is required.' Resize and theme-toggle legs are therefore correctly N-A. Interaction is genuinely exercised, never a still first paint: functional/prompt.md:29 and polish/prompt.md:18 define one-action timed observations (other person acts in an independent context, t0 only after the trigger succeeds, DOM read every 500 ms for 15000 ms without click/type/scroll/reload/navigate, void attempts repeat at most twice, met=false is final, 2000 ms settle before reading focus/scroll/draft, negatives watched for the full 15 s). That is Colderwater lessons 7 and 14 applied to every live leg. Live legs: functional/judge.toml hro_two_people (Mei's move and new card appear on Rafael's board), hro_messaging (reply arrives on the open conversation), hro_long_thread (scrolled-up place kept, notice shown, draft text and document.activeElement kept, unread until he goes to it), hro_unread_seen (counts rise by exactly two, open-at-newest does not raise, seen marks arrive on both sides); polish/judge.toml hro_pol_live_board (lines 47-54: scroll partway, open card, type a note, scroll offset within 2 px, focus, typing appends), hro_pol_live_thread, hro_pol_earlier_place (getBoundingClientRect().top preserved), hro_pol_failed_send (route abort or setOffline for one send), hro_pol_session_resume (second-tab sign-out, then Enter, sign-in prompt, draft survives). Optimistic move/put-back is exercised by clicking: hro_interview_places reads the real stage/place, the reason and document.activeElement after a refused move. Modifier-click holding is in app_context.md (lesson 8). Gates stay simple (lesson 4). Weak apps that would be caught: poll-on-focus only (the timed watch forbids interaction, so met=false); full re-render on poll (scroll/focus/draft legs fail); live board but no live unread/seen (hro_unread_seen timed legs); jump-to-top on loading earlier messages (hro_pol_earlier_place). DEFECT (a conforming app can fail). functional/prompt.md:29 (same text in polish/prompt.md:18): 'Never reload or navigate the watched page to confirm a negative; where a count or a seen mark is the negative, confirm it once more by reading it in a fresh independent context of the same person without opening that conversation.' The only seen-mark negative is functional/judge.toml:121 (hro_unread_seen, weight 3.5): step (4) and Bar 'Rafael's message ... is still not seen after only the Observer opened it'. The brief puts the seen mark on the message (hireops_rules.md section 6 'Seen': 'My most recent message shows whether it's been seen'), and the golden renders it only inside the open conversation: solution/app/public/js/threads.js:82 "n.receipt.textContent = m === last ? (m.id <= c.seenUpTo ? 'Seen' : 'Sent') : '';". The list rows (threads.js:36-63) carry name, status, preview and unread badge, with no seen state. So a fresh Rafael context cannot read the seen mark 'without opening that conversation'. With functional/prompt.md:33 'A step you skipped or did differently fails that criterion', a literal judge must fail hro_unread_seen for the golden and any conforming app: it either skips the confirmation or opens the conversation, which is doing it differently. Opening it as Rafael would not change the graded fact (a staff message is seen only when the candidate opens it), so the prohibition is unnecessary for seen marks. Impact is bounded: 3.5 of 61 functional weight (about 0.034 reward per run). It still makes Oracle < 1 plausible, and it is the 'conforming alternative that could fail' this row asks about. No configured judge run exists. raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The scripted golden workspace.json has groups such as 'unread counts per person, own messages never unread, seen only when the other side opens' and 'live board: another person's move arrives without reload; open card, note draft and focus kept', but it is not a judge run. So whether the judge actually performs the clicks and waits, and how it resolves this confirmation, is NOT EXERCISED. That is a further risk on its own.
counterexample: The golden, or any app that (as the brief implies) shows Seen/Sent only on the last own message inside the open conversation, runs hro_unread_seen step 4. After Aud opens the conversation, the judge watches Rafael's page for 15 s and it correctly still reads 'Sent'. The judge must then 'confirm it once more ... in a fresh independent context of the same person without opening that conversation'. The fresh Rafael conversation list shows no seen state, so the step cannot be performed. Under 'A step you skipped or did differently fails that criterion', the judge scores hro_unread_seen 0 although the app is correct. If instead it opens the conversation to read the mark, it 'did differently' and again fails.
suggested_fix: In the Timed observations paragraph of functional/prompt.md (and polish/prompt.md), limit the 'without opening that conversation' fresh-context confirmation to counts. For a seen-mark negative, say to confirm it in a fresh independent context of the sender by opening the conversation there, since the sender opening it does not change their own message's seen state. Then re-review hro_unread_seen and extend the golden harness to cover that leg.
